subject: Observability alliance: SSO alignment & SLA fallback plan
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah@datadog.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Nina Rao <nina@observabilityinc.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability alliance — SSO and SLA fallback questions

Hi Connor / Vanessa,

Thanks for the sync last week. As we prep the joint listing for Datadog + Grafana in Redwood’s partner catalog, two items came up from our security and commercial teams that I wanted to surface so we can align quickly:

1) SSO integration: Datadog will support SAML 2.0 and OIDC for the marketplace flow; we can provide the metadata and a test IdP. Grafana plans to use OIDC with a slightly different claim set. For customers who want a single-click experience across both tiles in the marketplace, we need a canonical attribute map and a discovery flow.

2) SLA & fallback: some joint customers asked that if one vendor’s managed service has an outage, Redwood’s hosted inference should automatically route telemetry to the other vendor’s exporter as a fallback for ingest continuity. Datadog legal asked for a short amendment that clarifies responsibilities when fallback routing occurs (data residency, retry windows, retained logs).

I attached a rough SSO diagram and a proposed SLA fallback matrix for review. Can we set a short working session this week to agree on the integration touchpoints and which side will own the onboarding docs?

Best,
Sarah
---
Sarah Li
Strategic Partnerships, Datadog
Attachments: sso-integration-diagram.png, proposed-sla-fallback-matrix.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@datadog.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul@grafana.com>, Nina Rao <nina@observabilityinc.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability alliance: SSO alignment & SLA fallback plan

Thanks Sarah — helpful summary. Quick notes from Redwood’s side:

- SSO: we can act as the discovery broker in the marketplace flow (i.e., we perform the initial IdP discovery and then redirect to vendor OIDC/SAML endpoints). That means we need a minimal, agreed claim set (email, org_id, role) and a small compatibility layer for name/role mapping. If Grafana wants OIDC-only, we can translate SAML assertions into the expected OIDC claims during the redirect flow.

- SLA fallback routing: we agree this should be transparent to customers and opt-in per tenant. We have two design constraints: 1) preserve data residency (no cross-region fallback unless customer opts in), and 2) make failure/retry behavior observable in the Redwood Console (metric and audit log entries).

Action items I propose:
- Short working session (45m) to nail the claim map and discovery sequence.
- Legal/commercial touchpoint to draft the fallback amendment language — Sarah, can your legal point someone to pair with Marcus?
- Implementation owner: Vanessa can lead Redwood’s integration plan and Nina can coordinate the consultancy advisory and test harness.

Available slots: Wed Mar 24 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu Mar 25 13:00-14:00 PT. Which works?

--
Connor O'Brien
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai

From: Paul Nguyen <paul@grafana.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Sarah Li <sarah@datadog.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Nina Rao <nina@observabilityinc.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability alliance: SSO alignment & SLA fallback plan

Thanks Connor — Thu 13:00 PT works for Grafana. A couple of clarifying points from our engineering lead: 

- Grafana will accept translated claims but prefers preserving the original subject_claim when present (for traceability). If Redwood does the SAML->OIDC translation, please include original_subject in the redirected payload.

- On the fallback routing: Grafana is okay with an opt-in fallback but requests a maximum retry window (we suggested 5 minutes) and a clear TTL for buffered telemetry. The proposed matrix looks fine but we need the amendment to state that ownership of buffered telemetry remains with the primary vendor unless explicitly transferred.

I'll be on the call Thu 25 Mar at 13:00 PT. Paul
---
Paul Nguyen
Head of Partnerships, Grafana

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@datadog.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul@grafana.com>, Nina Rao <nina@observabilityinc.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability alliance: SSO alignment & SLA fallback plan

Great — thanks everyone for quick alignment. Recap and next steps from Redwood operations: 

1) Working session confirmed: Thu Mar 25 13:00-13:45 PT (we'll use Redwood Meet link in the drive). Agenda: claim map, discovery flow, testing checklist. Nina to run the test harness plan.

2) Legal/commercial: Marcus, please coordinate with Sarah's counsel to draft a 1-page SLA fallback amendment. Key lines: opt-in per tenant; region-preserving by default; retry window = 5 minutes unless customer sets otherwise; buffered telemetry ownership stays with primary vendor unless customer authorizes transfer. We'll circulate a DocuSign stub after the call for redline.

3) Engineering: Connor and I will produce a short integration spec (SAML/OIDC mapping table + example payloads) within 3 business days. Paul — please confirm the field name for original_subject so we include it verbatim.

4) Deliverables & owners:
- Integration spec (Connor, Vanessa) — due Tue Mar 30
- Legal amendment draft (Marcus + Sarah legal) — due Tue Mar 30
- Test harness & runbook (Nina) — initial test plan by Mon Apr 5

Attached: draft SLA amendment (DocuSign stub) and the earlier SSO diagram.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
Attachments: docsign-sla-amendment.pdf, sso-integration-diagram.png
